minutes.headline: Board let the interim manager shift capital funds up to 25,000 per move; ARPA reallocation set for Nov 13.
minutes.summary: The board spent most of the meeting on reallocating ARPA money after Parks signalled it would return a large sum, hearing a list of emergency purchases from departments and schools. The finance director asked to redirect payroll-service money toward a Munis cloud migration, with broad support but no vote. The board voted to authorize internal capital reallocations and approved the language of Article 1 for the special town meeting, after announcing corrections to fincom and select board vote counts in the warrant booklet.

public_comment.topic: A board member reminded residents to check smoke and carbon monoxide detectors before the heating season.
Thanked the zoning board of appeals over an HOA shed dispute and described alleged harassment by a neighbor on Flat Hill Road and police not taking a report.

votes.motion: Ratify the interim town manager's appointment of Robin Nano as administrative assistant for the board of assessors.
Authorize the town manager to move funds in one transaction up to 25,000 (amended to drop the 50,000 total cap) between previously approved capital projects.
Approve the language of Article 1 (salary reserve and group health insurance) for the special town meeting.

Draft policy for one centralized card for incidental expenses and trainings.
A member and the chair floated one-time payments to eligible employees, to be proposed with numbers next meeting.

what_happened.line: The board voted unanimously to let the town manager move funds between approved capital projects, up to a set amount per transaction, with the total cap dropped.
The board voted unanimously to approve the language of Article 1, a salary reserve and group health insurance appropriation, for the special town meeting.
Most of the meeting went to reallocating ARPA money after Parks signalled it would return funds; departments and schools listed emergency purchases, with no vote.
A special ARPA workshop was set for Wednesday November 13 at 6:00 p.m., and the chair will circulate a spreadsheet of all departmental requests.
The finance director asked to redirect payroll-service money toward moving Munis to the cloud; support was broad, a written proposal was requested, and no vote was taken.

why_it_matters: Capital project money can now be shifted between approved projects by the town manager without a return to the board, which changes who decides when a project's budget is redirected.

Unspent ARPA money returned by Parks, the Munis cloud move and next year's pressures from software, retiree health insurance and salaries all draw on the same limited pool and the FY27 budget, and the ARPA choices are still open.
